ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; no refund to the rider; no account action against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
Driver-side cancellation means the fee can only stand through NS-0 → NS-1: cancelled_by = driver at 14:09:55 [F4], with the rider claiming no-show, so the charge is lawful only if every NS-1 element holds [NS-0][NS-1].

NS-1(i): the arrival was a genuine driver tap, not a platform auto-arrival — "I'm Here" at 14:06:15 [F6]; the timeline separately records a platform arrival at 14:03:20 [F5], but NS-1(i) is satisfied by the driver tap recorded in [F6] [NS-1]. NS-1(ii): at that tap the GPS placed the driver 178 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius [F6], with the closest approach over the whole stop being 40 m at 14:03:50 [F1]. NS-1(iii): after the 14:06:15 tap the driver stayed continuously within 200 m for 3 min 40 s (220 s) until the 14:09:55 cancellation, exceeding the 3:01 threshold, and the GPS trace runs from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation with no hole [F2][F6][F4] [NS-1]. The execution trace marks (i)(ii)(iii) as passed; all three conditions are therefore met and the $6.61 fee stands [F7] [NS-1].

The rider's real grievance is that 178–179 m is not the pinned entrance [F10]. That is a distance-of-arrival complaint the policy does not reach: NS-1 fixes arrival by the GPS radius at the moment of the tap, and the 200 m figure is a data-layer parameter, not a citable clause [NS-1]. The driver described his position ("at the side road") at 14:06 [F9]; the rider replied at 14:07 that she was at the entrance and could not see him [F10]; the driver then cancelled at 14:09 [F11][F4]. Because the arrival confirmation was made inside the radius and the wait was continuous, NS-2's failure branch is not triggered and no flag_account attaches on that basis [NS-2]. The driver's post-trip statement [F13] is not needed for the finding, since [F3][F6] already settle the elements; it is therefore not treated as contradicting the system record on any element the fee depends on [NS-1]. The already-charged $6.61 is a fixed recorded cancellation fee [F7][F4], so there is no multiplicative computation to perform; a fixed quoted fare unaffected by mileage [F8] also means RD-2 has no monetary application here [RD-2].

The profile records (rider 1 dispute, 0 upheld [F17]; driver 1 dispute, 1 upheld, no-show: 1 [F18]) are not used to decide the case; a profile never decides on its own, and RD-6 is not triggered because no refund is due and no RD-1 breach is recorded [RD-6][NS-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's 14:07 message shows only that she could not see the car; it does not rebut the system record that the driver's arrival tap was made 178 m from the pickup, inside the radius, at 14:06:15 [F6], nor the continuous 3 min 40 s wait within 200 m afterwards [F6]. NS-1(ii)/(iii) turn on the GPS record at the tap and the wait, not on the rider's sighting [NS-1].

The rider's advocate withdrew this concession; the point that 178–179 m is not the pinned entrance [F6][F3] is a distance-of-arrival grievance with no clause behind it. NS-1 fixes arrival by the GPS radius at the moment of the tap, and the 200 m figure is a data-layer parameter, not a citable provision [NS-1].

The completeness of the record [F5][F12] is accepted, but it establishes no G12 gap only; it does not create a refund ground. On the complete record the waiting period satisfies NS-1(iii) [F6][F4] [NS-1].
Fair weather and band-3 traffic with no incidents [F14][F15][F16] are irrelevant to NS-1, which turns solely on the tap, the radius at the tap and the continuous wait [F6] [NS-1].

The profile [F18] shows one dispute and one upheld in 90 days, not two; in any event a profile may not decide a case, and a flag_account requires a refund or a recorded RD-1 breach, neither of which arises here [F18][F17] [RD-6][NS-2].

The corroboration point is accurate for NS-1 [F2][F3][F12], but it does not resolve the rider's separate complaint that the car never reached the pinned entrance [F10]; the driver prevails because NS-1's elements are met, not because the statement [F13] adds anything [NS-1].

The rating and trip-count profile [F18] is irrelevant to the ruling; the outcome rests on the satisfied NS-1 conditions [F6][F4], and no flag_account arises because no refund or RD-1 breach is found [RD-6][NS-2].
